subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps (Aurora Health)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps (Aurora Health)

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call + proposed next steps so we have shared alignment. TL;DR: Aurora wants dedicated, isolated GPU capacity to support a production inference workload with strong latency SLOs and enterprise controls.

Pain points we heard:
- Spiky peak traffic (up to ~2k inference RPS during batch imports) causing tail-latency spikes on shared endpoints
- Multi-tenant isolation & compliance concerns — need guaranteed data separation and control-plane isolation for PHI workloads
- Predictable pricing and SLA for forecasting and procurement

Goals you stated:
- P95 generation latency <= 200ms for typical 512-token prompts under steady-state
- Capacity to handle concurrent peak traffic with headroom (target baseline throughput ~1.2k RPS, burst to 2k)
- Enterprise logging, audit trails, and SOC2 evidence for audits this fall

Proposed dedicated capacity plan (high level):
- Dedicated GPU pool: 8x A100 (reserved), with autoscale policy to add up to 12x A100 for burst windows
- Isolation: Dedicated VPC + customer-specific tenant on the runtime; optional private control plane for on-prem or VPC deployments
- Performance targets: warm-up and KV cache priming to meet P95 < 200ms in steady state; we will validate with synthetic replay of your traffic sample
- SLA target: 99.95% availability for the dedicated cluster; we’ll include an addendum for support response times and escalation path
- Security/compliance: attaching our SOC2 report and draft SLA addendum; we can run through your questionnaire next week

Attachments: redwood_aurora_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal + sizing), soc2_report_redwood_2025.pdf, redwood_sla_addendum.docx

Next steps / asks:
1) Please confirm procurement contact (I see procurement@aurorahealth.com — cc them if that’s correct)
2) Share a traffic sample JSON or tail logs (anonymized) so Dev can run a quick sizing replay — Dev, can you take this?
3) If pricing looks close, we’ll send a formal SOW + DocuSign link for an initial 6-month reserved commitment with monthly usage reconciliation
4) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive this week for throughput/benchmarking; proposed slots: Thu 10–11am PT, Fri 1–3pm PT

Thanks again — happy to jump on a quick call to walk the proposal.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0132

--

Attachment: soc2_report_redwood_2025.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
Attachment: redwood_sla_addendum.docx (DOCX, 120KB)

Ben — thanks for the clear recap and the materials. This captures the ask well. A few quick notes from our side:

- Procurement: procurement@aurorahealth.com is correct; looping them in for pricing and contracting.
- Compliance: we need the SOC2 report and any encryption/KMS details (can you confirm HSM/KMS integrations?) — received the SOC2 PDF, thank you.
- Sizing: the 8x A100 baseline with autoscale to 12 sounds reasonable; I’ll confirm with our infra team if they expect any larger burst windows (I’ll circle back by EOD Thursday).
- SLA: 99.95% is our target minimum for a contract; we’ll want clarity on crediting and what counts as downtime. Please ensure the SLA addendum addresses support response times for Sev 1/2.

We’d like the technical deep-dive with Dev next week — Thu 10am PT works for Alex + our infra lead.

Two asks from procurement:
1) Line-item pricing (reserved monthly + burst hourly rates + any minimum commitment)
2) DocuSign or draft SOW so procurement can start redlining ASAP

If you can send pricing + DocuSign today, procurement will prioritize review.

Appreciate it — Alex
Principal Cloud Architect | Aurora Health

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps (Aurora Health)

Quick internal note — tagging items for our legal/security review before we send the SOW to procurement:

1) SLA: confirm 99.95% availability wording and include explicit warm-up/priming window exclusions (we should propose a 2-hour warm-up during initial rollout to allow KV cache priming without SLA exposure).
2) Data isolation: ensure the proposal language calls out tenant-level isolation + optional private control plane for PHI workloads; add KMS/HSM integration details (we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS/HSM).
3) Redlines to watch: data egress/retention clauses (Aurora will likely push to limit retention and require deletion on termination) — add explicit retention/retention-delete process and export timeline.
4) Support: include 24/7 on-call for Sev 1, 2-hour initial response for Sev 1, 4-hour for Sev 2, with on-call escalation contacts (we’ll fill in names in the SLA addendum).

Ben — I’ll review the SLA addendum and SOC2 PDF and send comments directly into the DocuSign SOW if needed. Dev, please confirm feasibility of the replay plan and whether 8x A100 baseline + autoscale to 12 is sufficient for the traffic sample once Alex sends it.

Marissa
Head of Customer Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
